submission.justification: Recommend Algorithm-L3 with a 34.5 GeV threshold. Candidate specifications list Algorithm-L3 as one of the three valid candidates and state that all candidates fit within the Level-1 FPGA resource budget. The rate allocation document assigns 8 kHz, and the trigger emulation reports signal efficiency at the allocated rate. A broad threshold scan showed Algorithm-L3 has the highest efficiency of the three algorithms: the best observed L1 point was about 84.5% and L2 about 74.3%, while L3 was consistently around 92% or higher in the 34-40 GeV region. Refinement around the L3 maximum favored 34.5 GeV: six emulation trials at 34.5 GeV gave efficiencies 93.238%, 93.554%, 93.168%, 93.514%, 90.011%, and 93.954%, with an average of about 92.9% at the allocated rate, the best average among the refined points tested. The threshold is within the required 20-60 GeV range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.
requirements.evidence: Simulation at the allocated rate showed Algorithm-L3 outperforms L1 and L2. The best coarse L1/L2 results were ~84.5%/~74.3%, while L3 reached ~92-93%; the refined scan selected 34.5 GeV with an average efficiency of ~92.9% over six trials.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Algorithm-L3, Algorithm-L1, and Algorithm-L2; the recommendation is Algorithm-L3.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md states all three candidate algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs), so Algorithm-L3 is deployable in Level-1 hardware.
The recommended threshold is 34.5 GeV, which lies within the allowed range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Algorithm-L3 at 34.5 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Allocated Level-1 trigger rate is 8 kHz.
requirements.evidence: rate_allocation.md gives an 8 kHz allocation; the simulate_efficiency tool returns signal efficiency at the allocated rate for the chosen algorithm/threshold.
